title: Roman concessions — necessary-to-salvation truths clear in Scripture; rest at least virtually
source_text: XXII. Vicissim vero Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae nobis concedunt, omnia quae sunt omnibus simpliciter ad salutem necessaria, & quorum fides explicita a fidelibus singulis exigitur, in Scriptura clare & aperte haberi. Ac praeterea nobis largiuntur omnia quae necessaria sunt ad doctrinam fidei & morum in Scriptura saltem virtute & implicite contineri, & ex ea posse per bonam consequentiam deduci.
pass_a_gloss: Conversely the doctors of the Roman Church concede to us that all things which are simply necessary for salvation for everyone, and whose explicit faith is required of each of the faithful, are had clearly and openly in Scripture. And besides they grant us that all things necessary for the doctrine of faith and morals are at least contained in Scripture virtually and implicitly, and can be drawn from it by a good consequence.
pass_b_english: Rome concedes in turn: whatever is simply necessary for every person's salvation, and whose explicit faith each believer must hold, stands clear and open in Scripture.
They also grant that whatever is needed for faith-and-morals doctrine is at least in Scripture virtually and implicitly, and can be drawn by good consequence.

lemmas.gloss: simply necessary for salvation for everyone

choices.why: Marks Roman side giving ground on virtual containment.
